# NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (NIST AI 100-1)

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce |
| **Kind** | guidance (voluntary risk-management framework) |
| **Status** | NIST AI 100-1, issued January 2023 [p.2]; no later edition found; final |
| **Where to get it** | free public download, DOI https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1 [p.2]; publication number NIST AI 100-1 |
| **Binds whom** | no one — "voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic" [p.7]; "use of this framework is voluntary and organizations can utilize the suggestions according to their needs" [p.26] |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** It supplies a general-purpose vocabulary and
process structure (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) for AI risk management that NASA's own documents do
not define from scratch (our reading). It is organization-level and sector-agnostic, so it says
nothing about mission assurance, safety-critical software classes, or verification/validation —
NASA's documents own that ground. Its six "trustworthy AI characteristics" (valid and reliable; safe;
secure and resilient; accountable and transparent; explainable and interpretable; privacy-enhanced;
fair with harmful bias managed) [Sec. 3, p.17] are a useful outside checklist for naming what a risk
candidate is actually about (our reading).

**Key content for artificial intelligence / machine-learning assurance.**
- Four core functions — GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE — with GOVERN as a cross-cutting function
  infused throughout the other three (Sec. 5, Fig. 5 and surrounding text, pp.25-26).
- GOVERN function Table 1 lists subcategories such as GOVERN 1.1 (legal/regulatory requirements for
  AI), GOVERN 1.6 (inventory mechanisms for AI systems), GOVERN 1.7 (decommissioning/phase-out
  processes) (Table 1, Sec. 5.1, pp.27-28).
- Six trustworthy-AI characteristics, each given its own subsection (Sec. 3.1-3.7, pp.13-17): Valid
  and Reliable; Safe; Secure and Resilient; Accountable and Transparent; Explainable and Interpretable;
  Privacy-Enhanced; Fair with Harmful Bias Managed.
- Artificial intelligence / machine learning touchpoint: the entire document is about AI risk
  management — "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "algorithm," and "automat-" occur
  throughout; no need to isolate a bullet, the whole text is AI-focused.

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** Compares to `NASA-HDBK-2203` and `NPR_7150.2D` (software engineering
requirements and assurance handbook) — those documents are binding/guidance for NASA software
including AI-enabled software, while the AI RMF is a voluntary, non-NASA process framework with no
mission-assurance teeth (our reading).
